parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, no facility or border restriction, courts enforcing foreign gender recognition, policing consultative; but no gender-identity protection, hostile official rhetoric and thin recourse keep it mid-band.

State-imposed universal exposures: passport-marker refusals and misrepresentation risk, birth-sex facility bans criminal in four states, documented custody abuse; partly offset by working courts, hate-crime coverage, protective states.
No criminalisation, no facilities rule, no recorded targeting or violence, functioning rule-of-law microstate; only gaps are absent gender-identity protection and dated monarchical disapproval.

Felony same-sex statutes reach trans women read as male, no recognition, protection or recourse; but no prosecutions documented since 2013, a traditional third-gender role, and no trans-specific policing record.
Enforced criminalisation plus advocacy offence, documented presentation-based arrests, police sexual coercion, prison care denial, impunity; no protections and no marker route for an outed visitor.
